description:
How do architecture builds get from a build machine to production? Prototype and record, like examples/release_debian did for the C-compiler stance.

Scenarios:
- mix release built on CI, run on a different CPU (older x86, Graviton vs Ampere, Apple dev machine vs Linux prod).
- Docker buildx multi-arch (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64) from one Dockerfile.
- A mixed fleet behind one release: does one release carry several variants (portable + x86-64-v3, or per-arm level) and pick at load? Compare: several .so per module chosen by a load-time CPU check; one .so with function multiversioning (__attribute__((target_clones)) / ifunc, GCC and clang, glibc vs musl vs macOS support); leaving it to the user (one target per release).
- What the release contains and how big it gets; build time per variant; what a failed match looks like in logs.

Depends on .so files shipping in releases at all (defk-n8f).

Done when each scenario has a working recipe or a recorded reason it doesn't work, with a recommendation, in docs/research/simd.md and an examples/release_* directory if a recipe needs one.
title: Prototype: deploying architecture builds (releases, CI, Docker, mixed fleets)
